elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: HDI's inspection right is limited to “not more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: HDI must provide “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice” to the Company.
Inspection is limited to the Company's normal business hours.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The clause gives the inspection right to HDI's General Manager and does not require an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no confidentiality obligation on the person conducting the inspection.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no requirement to conduct inspections off-site where possible.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: HDI bears all fees incurred in connection with the inspection, without even an underpayment exception.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Although inspection is limited to relevant records, the clause does not prohibit HDI from directly accessing Company systems containing those records.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The once-per-twelve-month-period cap is at least as restrictive as once per year.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days' prior written notice, exceeding the 15-day requirement.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: HDI bears all inspection fees without an underpayment exception, which is more protective of the Company.
